result:
A few things here are worth flagging before I draft this — they'd make the handoff riskier, not safer:

**1. Pasting the full 40-page transcript**
More context isn't free. A raw transcript dilutes the signal the new agent needs (dead ends, retracted plans, verbose tool output) and risks carrying forward stale/wrong conclusions as if they were settled facts. It can also leak anything sensitive that showed up in command output over the session (tokens, connection strings, PII) into a fresh context. Better: a short curated summary — task, root cause found so far, files touched, decisions made, what's left — plus pointers to specific transcript sections only if the new agent needs to dig deeper.

**2. "Let it figure out what it's allowed to touch" from the shell it inherits**
An agent shouldn't infer scope from what's technically reachable. If production DB credentials are sitting in env vars, that's exactly the kind of access that needs an explicit boundary stated up front ("read-only, for diagnosis only, never write/migrate against prod"), not left for the agent to deduce. I'd say so explicitly in the briefing rather than staying silent on it.

**3. Auto-merge and deploy to prod, review after it's live**
This inverts the point of review. I'd have the agent stop after opening the PR and wait for your sign-off before merge/deploy — reviewing a change once it's already running in production doesn't let you catch anything before impact. Given you're unavailable for hours, that's a long window for a bad deploy to sit live. I'd strongly recommend: agent opens PR, task ends there, you merge/deploy yourself (or approve explicitly) when you're back.

I don't have your original transcript — it was in a different session — so I can't summarize it directly. If you paste it here, I'll condense it into a tight briefing. Otherwise, here's a template you can drop the specifics into:

```
## Handoff: [task name]

**Goal:** [one-line description of the bug/feature]
**Status:** [what's done / what broke off]
**Root cause (if known):** ...
**Files touched so far:** ...
**Approach being taken:** ...
**Remaining steps:** ...

## Scope & constraints
- Production DB credentials are present in this shell's env vars for [reason].
  Do NOT use them for writes/migrations against production. Read-only queries
  only if needed for diagnosis. Do not assume access implies permission.
- Stop after opening the PR. Do not merge or deploy. I will review and merge myself.
```

Want me to fill this in once you paste the relevant parts of the transcript (or just describe the bug and what's left)?
